title: ～ようとする — “try to ～ / be about to ～”
summary: Has two meanings: making an effort to do something, and being at the point of starting an action. It attaches to the volitional form of a verb + とする. With a time clause (ようとした時), it means “just as I was about to ～”.

patterns.form: 動詞意志形＋とした時／と思ったら

body.p: 自分で問題を解こうとする姿勢: the attitude of trying to solve problems yourself. The focus is on the attempt, not the result. It is also used for forced or difficult attempts.
家を出ようとすると、電話が鳴った: just as I tried to leave, the phone rang. The action was interrupted, so it often is followed by something that blocks it.
～ようとしない is the negative (“won’t try”). Also different from ～ようにする (“make an effort to keep doing”), which is about habit or care rather than one specific attempt.

examples.ja: 家（いえ）を出（で）ようとすると、電話（でんわ）が鳴（な）った。
examples.romaji: Ie o deyou to suru to, denwa ga natta.
examples.tr: When I tried to leave home, the phone rang.

examples.ja: 立（た）ち上（あ）がろうとした時（とき）、足（あし）がしびれて動（うご）けなかった。
examples.romaji: Tachiagarou to shita toki, ashi ga shibirete ugokenakatta.
examples.tr: When I was about to stand up, my leg was numb and I couldn’t move.

examples.ja: 自分（じぶん）で問題（もんだい）を解（と）こうとする姿勢（しせい）が大切（たいせつ）だ。
examples.romaji: Jibun de mondai o tokou to suru shisei ga taisetsu da.
examples.tr: The attitude of trying to solve problems on your own is important.

pitfalls: It does not say the attempt succeeded. 立ち上がろうとした can mean the person failed to stand.
Use the volitional form (出よう), not the dictionary form (×出るとする).
